patterns.sizing: Existing engine components; quantitative inputs still required

patterns.sizing: Existing engine components; quantitative inputs still required

patterns.sizing: Existing engine components; quantitative inputs still required

patterns.sizing: Existing engine components; quantitative inputs still required

questions.label: Does this activity answer, classify or translate text?
questions.why: Count the model work, not the number of screens or software services.
questions.obtain: Ask the application owner or inspect one complete request.

questions.label: Does it search documents or another information source?
questions.why: Retrieval adds supporting work; it is not automatically another text-generation call.
questions.obtain: Walk through a question that needs customer information.

questions.label: Does it choose actions, call tools or repeat model calls?
questions.why: One customer task may cause several model calls.
questions.obtain: Inspect a task trace or ask the developer how a task is completed.

questions.label: Does it process a collection of items by a deadline?
questions.why: A deadline converts work volume into a processing rate.
questions.obtain: Ask how many items arrive and when their results are needed.

questions.label: Does it process a continuous stream?
questions.why: Live sources may require sustained capacity and bounded delay.
questions.obtain: Count simultaneous sources; ask for their formats and processing rates.

questions.label: Does it create images, audio or video?
questions.why: Output size, duration and generation settings affect the work.
questions.obtain: Ask for a representative output and its required generation time.

questions.label: Does it fine-tune an existing model?
questions.why: Fine-tuning needs a training-method profile, not an inference estimate.
questions.obtain: Ask the ML team for the base model and adaptation method.

questions.label: Does it train from scratch or continue pretraining?
questions.why: Training volume, model and deadline determine a separate demand.
questions.obtain: Ask the ML team for the training campaign plan.

questions.label: Does it build or refresh a searchable document index?
questions.why: Document preparation and embeddings can be a separate scheduled workload.
questions.obtain: Ask how documents are added, changed and made searchable.

modifiers.label: Where will the model processing run?
modifiers.why: Only locally hosted work belongs in the local GPU estimate. Mixed placement needs a split into activities.
modifiers.obtain: Ask the application owner which services are external.

modifiers.label: How many model calls make up one customer task?
modifiers.why: Repeated calls expand demand; this is separate from users and requests.
modifiers.obtain: Inspect a representative task trace. A fixed count can be entered during sizing.

modifiers.label: When does this activity run?
modifiers.why: Different schedules do not prove that workloads never overlap.
modifiers.obtain: Ask the operations owner for the busy periods and deadlines.

modifiers.label: How is this activity related to the earlier activity selected below?
modifiers.why: Order, parallel work and conditional work have different consequences. This is a discovery relationship, not a compute multiplier.
modifiers.obtain: Walk through a typical task and an exception with its owner.

modifiers.label: May this activity share computing capacity?
modifiers.why: Dedicated workloads need separate capacity; sharing still needs schedule and isolation checks.
modifiers.obtain: Ask the service owner about customer isolation and operating policy.

policy: Anubis product taxonomy, not an industry standard. Unknown is never interpreted as no. Recognition is distinct from sizing qualification.
